I imagine you being there for everything. 

The exciting days. 

The boring days. 

The random trips. 

The family gatherings. 

The cafe visits that somehow last six hours for absolutely no reason. 

All of it. 

And I know for a fact it would be so much better. 

I would complain less. 

I would be less tired. 

I would probably spend more time smiling. 

And every random outing would instantly become more fun because you would be there. 

Today reminded me how much I want that. 

How much I want to experience all these ordinary moments with you. 

Because I think those are the moments that matter the most. 

Not the grand gestures. 

Not the special occasions. 

Just getting to live life together. 

And like I've told you, I think you would fit right in. 

You would be part of the family before the day even ended. 

So yes, today was long. 

Way too long. 

And yes, I am sorry I did not get to call you. 

But if there is one thing I took away from today, it is that I missed you every step of the way. 

And every place we went just made me wish you were there beside me. 

I miss you so much, baby. 

And I love you. 
Always. 
Regardless of everything.
159:
For the first time in a while, I was home the entire day. You would think that means I got to rest, but somehow I ended up feeling just as tired. Maybe it was the weather. Maybe it was the fact that everything felt so overwhelming from the moment I woke up.

It was bright. It was hot. It was humid. The air felt heavy.

Even doing nothing felt exhausting.

I do not know how to explain it properly, but everything just felt overstimulating today. The sunlight coming through the windows was too bright, the heat was too much, and even the simplest things felt like they were taking extra energy from me.

At one point, I genuinely thought I would rather go to the mall and just sleep there.

Which sounds ridiculous considering I just did that the other day and didn't like it.

Imagine being so tired of staying at home that your solution is to go sleep in a public place.

But honestly, at least the mall has air conditioning.

At least it is cool.

At least I would not feel like I am slowly melting into the floor.

That is how hot it felt today.

And because I was home the whole day, I had a lot of time to think.

Which is both a good thing and a bad thing.

Because every time I found myself staring at the ceiling, or scrolling through my phone, or doing absolutely nothing, my mind somehow ended up going back to you.

I kept thinking about how much I miss you.

I kept thinking about how excited I am to finally go home.

Not even because of the place itself.

But because home means comfort.

It means familiarity. It means my room. It means turning on my air conditioner and finally feeling like I can breathe again.

And most importantly, it means getting to spend time with you properly.

I think that is what I miss the most right now.

Our normal days.

Our routine.

The simple things that do not seem special until they are suddenly gone.

Calling you whenever I want. Watching movies together. Talking about random things. Listening to your stories. Hearing you laugh. Hearing you get sleepy. Staying there until you eventually drift off.

Those moments have become such a normal part of my life that when they are missing, I notice it immediately.

And I noticed it today.

Because while I was sitting there feeling tired and overheated, all I could think about was how nice it would be if I was spending that time with you instead.

I kept imagining finally getting back home, turning on the AC, laying down comfortably, calling you, and just existing together for a while.

Nothing complicated. Nothing grand.

Just us.

The way I like it. The way I miss it.

And honestly, I think that is one of the biggest signs that I love you.

Because when I imagine comfort, somehow you are always part of it.

When I imagine resting, you are there.

When I imagine peace, you are there.

When I imagine the end of a long exhausting day, you are there too.

You have become such a big part of what feels like home to me.

So yes, today was hot.

It was bright.

It was tiring.

It was one of those days where everything felt a little too much.

But it also reminded me of something.

It reminded me how much I miss my baby.

And how excited I am for the moment I can finally settle down at the end of the day, call you, hear your voice, and spend time with you until you inevitably fall asleep on me.

I miss you so much, baby.

And I love you, of course.
Always.
Regardless.
160:
Today was not much better than yesterday.

I woke up feeling the exact same way.

Still hot.

Still bright.

Still noisy.

There were people talking already, things happening around the house, and I just remember laying there wishing for a little bit of silence.

I think what makes it harder is that I am so used to waking up differently. Back home, my mornings are usually quiet. My room is dark, the air feels calmer, and the only thing I really hear are the birds outside. It is peaceful in a way that I probably took for granted before this trip.

Here, it feels like the day starts at full volume.

The sun is already shining through everything, people are already moving around, conversations are already happening, and somehow my brain has to catch up to all of it the moment I open my eyes.

So I was still feeling a little overwhelmed today.

Still feeling everything all at once.

Still wishing for a little quiet.

Still missing my normal routine.

But then we called.

And things got easier.

That is honestly becoming a pattern now.

It does not matter if I am tired, overwhelmed, stressed, overstimulated, or just having an off day. The moment I hear your voice, things feel a little lighter.

Not because all my problems magically disappear.

They don't.

The heat is still there.

The noise is still there.

Everything around me is still happening.

But somehow I stop focusing on all of it.

Instead, I focus on you.

On whatever random thing you are talking about.

On your reactions.

On your stories.

On your laugh.

And before I know it, I am smiling instead of being annoyed.

You are such a good distraction, baby, hihi kiss ko.

The best kind.

The kind that makes me forget everything else for a while.

Today was also a busy day because it was my father's birthday.

So naturally, there was a lot to do around the house.

I ended up helping with the preparations, cutting vegetables, helping with the food, running around doing little tasks here and there. I felt like I never stopped moving.

Which is funny because I came here thinking I would get some rest.

Apparently not.

But despite being busy, it was still nice helping out.

There is something special about seeing everyone come together for occasions like this.

Everyone doing their part.

Everyone contributing something.

Everyone trying to make the day feel special.

And I was happy to be part of that.

The only thing that made me a little sad was that you did not get to greet my father.

I know you would have if you could.

But the power outage had other plans.

Of all the times for the electricity to disappear, it had to happen then.

And not only did it stop you from greeting him, it also ended our call.

Which honestly sucked.

Because I never really feel ready for our calls to end.

Especially when I already miss you as much as I do lately.

But despite that, I am still happy with how we left things.

The call ended softly.

It ended well.

And honestly, that is what matters most.

Sometimes things do not go exactly how we want them to.

Sometimes power outages happen.

Sometimes plans get interrupted.

Sometimes time gets cut short.

But as long as we still find our way back to each other, I think we will be okay.

And before I end this letter, I just want to say that I am really happy for you, baby.

Continue doing the things you love.

Continue finding things that make you happy.

Continue growing into the person you want to become.

Continue choosing yourself too.

Because seeing you happy genuinely makes me happy.

Seeing you excited about something makes me excited too.

And seeing you enjoy your life, even from far away, is something I will always support.

I know I say it a lot, but I am so proud of you.

For everything you do.

For everything you are.

And for the way you keep showing up every single day.

I miss you so much.

I love you so much.

And no matter how hot, bright, noisy, or overwhelming these days get, they always become a little easier when I get to spend them with you.

I love you baby.
Always.
Regardless.
161:

Eating.

Excited to feel the comfort of familiar surroundings.

I miss watching movies with you.

I miss talking about absolutely everything and absolutely nothing at the same time.

I miss those conversations that somehow start with one topic and end somewhere completely different hours later.

I miss hearing you get sleepy.

I miss staying up together.

I miss falling asleep knowing you are there.

These past few days have made me appreciate those little things even more.

Because when they're taken away, even for a short while, I realize just how much they mean to me.

So while today was busy, while it was short, and while we did not get as much time together as I wanted, I'm still grateful.

Grateful that we found time anyway.

Grateful that I got to hear your voice.

Grateful that I got to stay with you while you slept.

And grateful that tomorrow, I finally get to come home...

To you. Chereret.

I can't wait to spend time with you properly again, baby.

Let's watch movies.

Let's talk for hours.

Let's laugh at stupid things.

Let's tell each other about our days.

And let's fall asleep together again.

I miss you so much.

I LOVE YOU SO MUCH.
ALWAYS.
REGARDLESS.
162:

I missed my own bed.

I missed my routine.

I missed being able to just lay down and do absolutely nothing.

And most importantly, I missed the feeling of being comfortable.

The whole trip was fun, and I am grateful for it, but there is just something different about coming home after being away for a while. Everything feels familiar again. Everything feels calmer. It is like your body finally realizes it can relax.

I was also really excited because I thought I would get to spend a lot of time with you today.

I spent the last few days looking forward to it.

Looking forward to finally being home, finally being comfortable, and finally getting to have one of our usual days again.

But life had other plans.

We did not really get to spend as much time together as I expected.

Not because anything was wrong.

Not because we did not want to.

We were just both tired.

You were tired.

I was tired.

And sometimes that is just how things are.

There are days where all the excitement catches up to you, all the responsibilities catch up to you, and all you really want is rest.

So instead of having some grand movie marathon or staying up talking until sunrise, we just slept.

And that was okay.

Because even if our time together was short, I was still happy.

Happy that I got to hear your voice.

Happy that I knew you were resting.

Happy that I was finally back home while talking to my baby again.

I think one thing this trip taught me is how much I appreciate our normal days.

The simple ones.

The ones where nothing special happens.

The ones where we just watch something together.

The ones where we talk about random things.

The ones where we fall asleep on call without even realizing it.

Those moments do not seem extraordinary while they are happening, but when you spend days away from them, you realize how much they actually mean.

And now that I am finally back, I am excited for all of it again.

The movie nights.

The random conversations.

The teasing.

The backreading.

The sleepy calls.

The moments where we talk about absolutely nothing and somehow still have fun.

All of it.

So even though today was shorter than I hoped, and even though we were both too tired to really do much, I am ending the day feeling grateful.

Grateful that I am home.

Grateful that you are here.

Grateful that after all the travelling, all the heat, all the exhaustion, and all the chaos, I finally get to return to the person who feels the most like home to me.

Get some rest, baby.

I know we are both tired.

Tomorrow is another day, and hopefully one where we get a little more time together.

I missed you so much.

And now that I am finally home, I plan on making up for all that lost time.

I love you bb.
163:

I finish whatever I have to do during the day, 
and by the time we finally get each other, 
we are both already running on the last few percent of our batteries.

Another movie.

Another conversation.

Another few hours together before sleeping.

Instead of deep conversations about life, we are both half asleep trying to form complete sentences.

I really do.

Because at the end of the day, it has never been about the activity itself.

It was never just about the movies.

Or the conversations.

Or finding something to do.

It was always about you.

Just having you there.

Just hearing your voice.

Just knowing we are sharing a small part of our day together before it ends.

That has always been enough for me.

Because life is busy.

You are busy.

I am busy.

You come home tired from taking care of little kids all day.

I get tired from my own responsibilities too.

And yet somehow, even when we have almost no energy left, we still find our way back to each other.

Even if all we do is sleep.

I think that is kind of beautiful.

Because anybody can spend time together when everything is easy.

But these days are different.

These are the days where we are exhausted.

Where we barely have energy.

Where our eyes are fighting to stay open.

And somehow we still choose each other.

You still call me.

I still stay.

You still fall asleep knowing I am there.

And I still smile every time it happens.

Today was exactly that.

There were no movies.

No deep talks.

No long discussions about the future.

No dramatic moments.

Just sleep.

Lots of sleep.

And honestly, I would not change a thing.

Because hearing your sleepy voice before you drift off has become one of my favorite parts of the day.

Hearing you get quieter.

Hearing your responses become shorter.

Hearing you slowly lose the battle against sleep.

It is cute every single time.

And even when we are not talking, there is something comforting about knowing you are there.

Sometimes I think that is one of my favorite things about us.

We do not always need something happening.

We do not always need entertainment.

We do not always need a plan.

Sometimes we can just exist together.

Sometimes we can just rest.

Sometimes we can just sleep.

And somehow it still feels meaningful.

It still feels like quality time.

It still feels like us.

So even if this has become our new normal lately, I am okay with it.

Because I know it will not be like this forever.

Eventually practicum will slow down.

Eventually schedules will line up better.

Eventually we will have movie nights again.

Eventually we will have those long conversations again.

But for now, if all we can give each other is our sleepy selves at the end of a long day, then that is more than enough for me.

Because I love every version of you.

The energetic version.

The talkative version.

The clingy version.

And especially the sleepy version.

So thank you for showing up today, even when you were tired.

Thank you for spending what little energy you had left on me.

And thank you for letting me be part of your nights, even when all we do is sleep.

I love it.

And more importantly, I love you. 
Always. 
Regardless.
164:
Today was special. 

Not because something huge happened, not because we spent the whole day together, and not because we did anything extraordinary. In fact, it was a pretty simple day. 

We managed to squeeze in a movie before my baby started getting sleepy again. 

Which honestly was not surprising. 

These past few weeks, you have been working so hard. Between practicum, waking up early, coming home tired, and still trying your best to show up for me every day, I can see how exhausted you are. Even through a screen, I can see it.  

So when you asked me to wake you up after an hour, I said okay. 

And I did. 

Like the responsible boyfriend that I am tnx. 

But when I woke you up, all I got was a sleepy baby telling me she was still tired. 

And I already knew where that was going. 

So I just let you sleep. 

Because how could I not? 

You sounded so cute. 

So sleepy. 

So comfortable. 

And at that point, getting rest was probably the best thing for you anyway. 

My poor hardworking baby. 

Today was also our friend's fiesta celebration, so later on I had to go out and attend. It was fun seeing everyone again, eating together, talking, and just enjoying the day. But what I did not expect was how emotional the whole thing would make me feel. 

Because today was the exact same day last year that I saw you again. 

After three whole years. 

Three years baby. 

When I thought about that, I genuinely had to stop for a moment. 

Because standing there today, surrounded by the same people, in the same celebration, I suddenly remembered everything. 

I remembered seeing you again. 

I remembered that exact moment. 

And the first thing I thought was, 
Wow, she still looks the same. 

Pretty. 

Cute. 

Beautiful, even. 

Just like I remembered. 

It is funny because even after three years, I recognized you immediately. 

And yet at the same time, it felt so different. 

Because before that day, you were mostly memories. 

Old conversations. 

Old photos. 

Old feelings. 

Old versions of ourselves. 

And then suddenly you were standing right there in front of me again. 

Real. 

Present. 

And somehow still making me nervous. 

I remember feeling so anxious that day. 

Not because I didnt wanna see you. 

Quite the opposite. 

I wanted to see you so badly. 

But I was scared. 

Because before you left years ago, we never really got closure. 

We had that unfinished argument. 

We drifted apart. 

And then life happened. 

So when I saw you again, part of me genuinely wondered if you were still mad at me. 

I remember overthinking everything. 

Wondering how you felt. 

Wondering if things would be awkward. 

Wondering if we would even be able to talk normally. 

And now looking back, it is so funny. 

Because if somebody told that version of me what would happen next, I probably wouldnt have believed them. 

If somebody told me that one year later, I would be writing letters to you every night. 

That we would spend almost every day together calling. 

That you would become my safe place. 

That I would fall in love with you all over again. 

That you would become the person I miss every single day. 

That you would become my home. 

I genuinely would have laughed. 

And yet here we are. 

Exactly one year later. 

I think that is what makes today feel so special. 

Because today was not just another fiesta. 

Today marks the day everything started again. 

The second beginning of our story. 

The day two people who thought their chapter was over somehow found their way back to each other. 

And I think that is beautiful. 

Because life could have gone so many different ways. 

We could have stayed strangers. 

We could have stayed a memory. 

We could have remained part of each other's past. 

But somehow, out of all the possibilities, we found our way back. 

And now, one year later, I am sitting here missing you while writing this. 

Life is funny sometimes. 

But I wouldnt change a thing. 

Because meeting you again was one of the best things that ever happened to me. 

It gave us another chance. 

Another beginning. 

Another opportunity to love each other better than before. 

And every day since then has been worth it. 

So while my baby spent most of today sleeping, and while we did not get to spend as much time together as I wanted, I am still ending this day feeling grateful. 

Grateful for today. 

Grateful for one year ago. 

Grateful that you came back into my life. 

And grateful that one year later, I still get to call you mine. 

I love you more than you know, my sweet girl.
165:
Today is Sunday, which means I did what every good boyfriend should do.

I went to church.

I thought it was going to be a normal Sunday.

Attend Mass.

Pray.

Listen.

Go home.

The usual.

But apparently today had other plans.

Because after so many Sundays of going to church, after all the times I have sat through Mass hoping it would happen, I finally saw your parents there.

You have no idea how surprised I was.

I had to do a double take.

I know how rare it is for me to actually run into them there, and I have been telling you for the longest time that I really wanted to meet them, or at the very least get the chance to bless them.

Not because I am trying to score points (?).

Not because I am trying to be impressive (?).

But because its a sign of respect, and it mattered to me.

So the moment I realized it was actually them, I knew I could not let the opportunity pass.

There was no way I was going home and telling you, "Yeah, I saw your parents, but I did not say hi."

Absolutely not.

So I waited for the right moment, gathered my courage, and made sure I got the chance to bless them.

And I did.

Finally.

It was such a simple interaction, but it made me happy.

Standing there talking to your parents, even for a brief moment, felt nice hehe.

Because the whole time I had this funny thought in the back of my mind,
they have absolutely no idea that Im dating their daughter.

Which somehow made the whole thing even cuter.

There I was, being respectful, blessing them, talking normally, while secretly thinking,

"If only you knew."

I was just happy.

Happy that I finally got to meet them.

Happy that I got to show them respect.

Happy that I didnt miss the opportunity.

Because who knows when the next chance will be.

But beyond that, something else stuck with me.

While I was watching them together during Mass, I could not help but think about us.

I know that sounds cheesy.

But its true.

Seeing your parents there, attending church together, made me imagine what that would be like for us someday.

Going to church every Sunday together.

Sitting beside each other during Mass.

Sharing knowing glances whenever the priest says something funny.

Holding hands on the walk back.

Arguing over where we should eat afterward.

Then ending up on a little Sunday dinner date somewhere.

Nothing extravagant.

Nothing fancy.

Just us.

A simple routine.

A quiet tradition.

The kind of thing that seems ordinary until you realize those ordinary moments are actually the ones that matter most.

And honestly, baby, I would love that.

I would love waking up on a Sunday knowing I get to spend the morning with you.

I would love going to church together.

I would love seeing you dressed up and pretending not to notice how pretty you look.

I would love walking beside you afterward while we figure out what to eat.

I would love all of it.

Because when I think about the future, it is never really the grand moments that come to mind first.

It is the small things.

The routines.

The traditions.

The everyday moments.

The things couples do without even thinking about them.

And somehow, seeing your parents together today reminded me of that.

It reminded me that love is not just found in big gestures.

Sometimes it is found in showing up every Sunday.

Sometimes it is found in sitting beside the same person year after year.

Sometimes its found in sharing a meal afterward.

And I think thats beautiful.

So yes, today was just another Sunday.

But it was also the day I finally got to meet your parents.

The day I finally got to bless them.

The day I got a little glimpse of something I hope we get to have someday.

And I am not gonna lie, that thought made me smile the entire way home.

I miss you baby.

And I cant wait for the day we get to attend Mass together, walk out side by side, and go on our little Sunday dinner dates afterward.

I think that sounds pretty perfect.

I wuv you.
166:
Today was one of those days where nothing really went wrong, but nothing really went the way I wanted either.

I spent a good part of the day preparing for my job interview. I was reviewing things, fixing little details, thinking about possible questions, and trying to make sure I was as ready as possible. Honestly, I was taking it seriously because I genuinely want this to go well.

But by the time I need to go, I just didnt feel like myself.

I cant really explain it properly, but I was not feeling my best physically, and I knew it would affect how I presented myself. So instead of forcing it, I made the decision not to go today and just attend tomorrow instead.

At first I felt a little bad about it because I had already spent all that time preparing, but the more I thought about it, the more I realized it was probably the right decision. If Im going to show up for something important, I want to do it properly. I want to be present, confident, and at my best, not tired, sluggish, and wishing I had given myself another day.

So I guess all that preparation was not really for nothing after all. If anything, it means I get another day to polish things up and walk in tomorrow feeling more prepared than I would have today.

Still, your baby was locked in all day for an interview that he chose not to attend.

Anyway.

The betrayal.

The disrespect.

The audacity.

Jokes aside, I am glad you liked the letter.

That made me happy.

I put a lot of thought into those, and knowing that they mean something to you always makes writing them worth it.

But baby,
You could have at least waited for me.

Half the fun is watching your reactions.

I wanted to see which parts made you smile.

Which parts made you blush.

Which parts made you roll your eyes and call me dramatic.

Which parts made you go, "aww"

I feel like I missed out on the best part.

So now I am going to need a full reaction recap.

Those are the rules.

I dont make them.

After that, the day got even quieter.

My baby started feeling sleepy.

Which to be fair, has become pretty normal lately.

And I was not far behind.

Because if Im being completely honest, I just did not feel that great today.

Nothing serious.

Nothing specific.

Just one of those days where I felt off.

The kind of day where you wake up and your energy never really arrives.

The kind of day where everything feels slower than usual.

Where motivation decides to disappear.

Where you look back at the day and feel like you did not accomplish much.

That was me today.

I felt unproductive.

I felt sluggish.

And even though I had things I wanted to do, I could not really find the energy for them.

So when my baby got sleepy, I ended up sleeping too, for 4 hours at that.

Maybe that is exactly what we both needed.

Sometimes resting is productive too.

Im trying to remind myself of that.

Not every day has to be exciting.

Not every day has to be full of accomplishments.

Sometimes surviving the day and getting enough rest is enough.

And maybe today was one of those days.

So while I wish I had more energy, while I wish I got to watch you read the letter in real time, I am still ending the day grateful.

Grateful that tomorrow is another chance.

Another chance for the interview.

Another chance to feel more like myself.

Another chance to be productive.

And another chance to spend time with my baby.

Hopefully with less sleeping and more letting me watch your reactions to my letters.

I love you baby.

And even on the slower days, I am happy that I get to spend them with you.
167:
Today was a quiet one.

We did not really do much today, and honestly, that was okay.

I had somewhere I needed to be, and my baby also had to sleep early because she had something important the next morning. So before we even got the chance to think about watching a movie or staying up talking for hours, we already knew today was going to be a short one.

And that is completely fine.

I think that is one thing I have been learning more and more lately.

Not every day has to be packed with things for it to be a good day.

Not every call has to last for hours.

Not every moment together has to be exciting.

Sometimes life is just busy.

Sometimes responsibilities come first.

Sometimes we only get a small window of time before one of us has to leave again.

And I think there is something beautiful about the fact that we still choose to spend that little bit of time together anyway.

Because we easily could have said,"ill talk to u tmr"

But we never really do that.

We always try to find time for each other, no matter how small it is.

Even if it is only for a few minutes.

Even if one of us is already sleepy.

Even if the other has somewhere to be.

We still show up.

And I think that says a lot about us.

Today reminded me that quality has always mattered more than quantity.

Of course I would love to spend the entire day with you.

I would watch three movies with you.

Talk until sunrise.

Listen to you ramble about anything that comes to your mind.

Tease you every chance I get.

And somehow still complain that the day was too short.

But even when we cannot have all of that, I still leave our calls happy.

Because as cheesy as it sounds, hearing your voice is enough to make my day feel complete.

Sometimes I do not even care what we are talking about.

Sometimes we are just updating each other about our day.

Sometimes we sit there quietly.

Sometimes we are both tired.

But hearing you on the other side of the call brings a kind of peace that I cannot really explain.

It makes everything feel okay.

It makes the busy days feel lighter.

It makes the distance feel a little smaller.

And I think that is one of my favorite things about loving you.

You do not have to do anything extraordinary.

You do not have to entertain me.

You do not have to stay awake longer than you should.

Just knowing you are there is enough.

Just hearing your voice for a little while is enough.

That is all it takes for me to think that today was a good day.

So even though today was short, and even though we barely had time before we both had to go back to our own responsibilities, I am still ending the day with a smile.

Because I got to spend a little piece of it with you.

And lately, I have realized that even the smallest pieces of time with you are worth more to me than hours spent doing anything else.

I hope tomorrow is a little less busy for both of us.

I hope we get a little more time.

But if not, that is okay too.

Because as long as I get to hear my baby, even just for a little while, my day always feels complete.

I love you, baby.
168:
After what felt like so many days of only getting little pieces of each other, we finally got to spend proper time together again.

No rushing because one of us had somewhere to be.

No ending the call early because you were too sleepy.

No trying to squeeze everything we wanted to do into thirty minutes.

It was just us.

I missed that so much.

We finally continued one of our many unfinished series.

At this point, we have so many unfinished shows that I do not even know how we are ever going to finish all of them. My baby gets interested in one thing, then another, then another, and suddenly we have a whole library waiting for us. Its so you, and I think its cute.

We watched together, ate together, laughed at the little scenes, paused from time to time just to talk about something random, and it reminded me of how much I missed our normal days.

There was no pressure today.

No heaviness.

No misunderstandings.

Just the kind of peace that I always look forward to whenever I get to spend time with you.

I think thats what I have been missing the most these past few weeks.

Not necessarily the movies.

Not even the amount of time.

Just this feeling.

This feeling of everything being okay.

Where we can just exist together without worrying about anything else.

Where the world feels quiet for a little while because I get to spend it with my favorite person.

Those are always my favorite days.

And somewhere in the middle of everything, we ended up having one of those conversations that somehow starts so casually but turns into something much deeper.

We started talking about the future.

About us.

About all the things we want to experience together.

About the life we have been dreaming about for so long.

Those conversations always do something to me.

They make me smile because they remind me that we are dreaming about the same future.

That we are both working toward something bigger than today.

That all this distance, all the waiting, all the missing each other, is for a reason.

It is because we believe theres something waiting for us at the end of all this.

And every time we talk about that future, I feel my intentions becoming even stronger.

It reminds me why Im working so hard.

Why I wanna build a career.

Why I wanna become a better man.

Why I keep choosing patience even when this distance hurts.

Because every step I take now feels like a step toward you.

Toward the life we always imagine.

Toward finally closing the distance between us.

Toward finally waking up and not having to calculate time zones anymore.

But if Im being honest, our conversation also stirred something inside me.

Not because of anything you did wrong.

Not because I suddenly doubted us.

It was more complicated than that.

It reminded me that the future is not something we can hold in our hands yet.

There are still things outside of our control.

Still uncertainties.

Still sacrifices that have to be made before we can finally get where we want to be.

And I realized just how scary that can feel sometimes.

Because when you love someone this deeply, the future starts to feel incredibly precious.

You become protective of it.

You become afraid of the thought that life could take unexpected turns before you ever get the chance to live the dreams you've been building together.

For a moment, I felt my heart get a little shaken.

Not because my love became smaller.

If anything, it was the opposite.

It was because I realized how much I have invested my heart into this future with you.

How real it has become in my mind.

How badly I want to wake up one day and realize we finally made it.

I guess loving someone this much also means allowing yourself to become vulnerable.

Because the more someone means to you, the more you realize how much there is to lose.

And maybe that is okay.

Maybe love is supposed to feel that way sometimes.

Not because it is built on fear, but because it is built on something that matters enough to protect.

Despite those feelings, there is one thing that never changed throughout our conversation.

My intention.

If anything, it became even stronger.

Stronger to keep working.

Stronger to become someone worthy of the future we talk about.

Stronger to keep choosing you, even on the days where the future feels far away.

Because no matter how uncertain life can be, there is one thing I am certain of.

I love you.

And every dream I have about the future still has you in it.

Today reminded me that the road ahead might not always be simple, but it also reminded me why I am willing to walk it in the first place.

Because at the end of it, I hope it is your hand I get to hold.

I love you baby.
Always.
Regardless.
169:
I was out for almost the entire day, and by the time I got home, I genuinely felt like I had been running around nonstop. I had errands to do early in the morning, one thing after another, and before I even realized it, half the day had already disappeared.

I was not in the best mood.

I lacked sleep.

I was already tired before the day even properly started.

Everything felt a little louder than usual, people everywhere, traffic, the heat, constantly moving from one place to another. Those are the kinds of days that usually drain me so quickly. found myself getting annoyed over little things, not because they were big problems, but because I simply did not have the energy for them.

But despite all of that, I still wanted to make time for you.

I knew I had to go out again later to finish the rest of my errands, but before that, I managed to squeeze in around two hours with my baby.

And somehow, those two hours completely changed my day.

It is honestly crazy how much influence you have over my mood without even trying.

Before the call, I was exhausted.

My social battery was gone.

I just wanted the day to be over already.

Then you answered.

And suddenly I found myself laughing.

Teasing you.

Smiling at the smallest things you said.

Making stupid jokes.

Listening to you talk.

And for those two hours, it was like everything outside stopped existing for a while.

The tiredness was still there physically, of course.

My legs were still tired.

My eyes still wanted sleep.

But mentally, I felt lighter.

It is funny because you did not really do anything extraordinary.

You were just being you.

And somehow, that has always been enough.

You have this way of making even my busiest days feel softer.

You have this way of reminding me that no matter how stressful the day gets, I still have something to look forward to.

Sometimes I think about how strange that is.

How one person can completely shift the direction of someone else's day.

I can spend hours outside feeling irritated by everything, then spend a little time with you, and suddenly I am okay again.

Not because all my problems disappear.

They do not.

But because you make carrying them feel a little easier.

Because you remind me that after all the errands, all the responsibilities, all the tiring parts of the day, I still get to come home to you.

Even if "coming home" right now just means hearing your voice through a call.

I think that is one of my favorite things about us.

You have unknowingly become my safe place.

The person I naturally look for after a long day.

The person I want to tell everything to.

The person who can make me forget how exhausting the world felt just a few minutes before.

I do not think you even realize how often you do that for me.

And I hope you know that I never take it for granted.

Because those little moments, the random conversations, the teasing, the laughter, they do so much more for me than you probably think.

They remind me that I am loved.

They remind me that I am not carrying everything alone.

And they remind me why, no matter how busy life gets, I will always try to make time for you.

Because somehow, even just two hours with my baby can completely change an entire day.

Thank you for being that kind of person for me.

Thank you for making the exhausting days feel a little less exhausting.

And thank you for being my favorite part of even the busiest days.

I love you baby.
Always.
Regardless.
170:
Today was my twin cousins' graduation celebration, so of course we had to celebrate such a big milestone. I am happy for them. Graduating is something worth celebrating, and I am proud that they finally reached that point after all their hard work.

I ended up arriving a little later than everyone else because I had a few things to finish beforehand, and by the time I got there, everyone was already almost drunk.

I kind of expected it.

It is a celebration after all.

But walking into that energy while completely sober was definitely an experience.

Still, I told them I would come, and I always try my best to keep my word, so I stayed, talked with everyone, laughed here and there, and enjoyed the little moments as much as I could.

After that, we all decided to go clubbing.

I thought it was going to be more fun than it actually was.

Maybe it was because I barely drank.

Maybe it was because I was just tired.

Or maybe I have simply reached the point where I enjoy quieter moments more than loud ones.

Whatever the reason was, it just was not as exciting as I imagined.

Instead of feeling like I was partying, I felt more like I was babysitting everyone.

Making sure nobody wandered off.

Checking if everyone was okay.

Watching people who could barely stand straight somehow convince themselves they could dance.

It was funny to watch, but it also made me realize I was probably the most responsible person there for once.

While everyone else was caught up in the music and the drinks, I found myself just observing everything around me.

And, of course, I started thinking about you.

I saw so many couples together.

Some were dancing.

Some were just standing there talking despite the loud music.

Some were laughing over whatever.

And I caught myself smiling because the only thought that came into my head was,

"We would look so cute here together."

Not because I suddenly want us to become club people.

You know me.

But because I realized that it does not really matter where we are.

Whether it is church, the beach, the grocery store, a café, a wedding, a birthday party, or even a club, somehow my mind always finds a way to picture you beside me.

I could already imagine teasing you if a funny song came on.

Holding your hand while we walked through the crowd so we would not lose each other.

Finding a quieter corner just to talk because you know I would rather hear your voice than the music anyway.

I think that is what I missed the most tonight.

Not the drinks.

Not the party.

Just you.

Because I have realized that places do not really make memories for me.

The people I experience them with do.

And I know, without a doubt, that tonight would have been so much more fun if you were there beside me.

We probably would have laughed at everyone.

Made fun of each other's dance moves.

Taken the cutest pictures.

And eventually gotten tired, left early, and gone somewhere to eat instead.

That honestly sounds more like us.

So even though today was not exactly how I imagined it would be, I am still grateful I got to celebrate with everyone.

I am proud of my cousins.

I am glad I kept my promise and showed up.

And somehow, even on a night surrounded by so many people, I still found another reason to miss my baby.

I hope one day we get to experience all these random little moments together.

Because I already know that no matter where we are, if I am with you, that is probably where I will have the most fun.

I love you baby.
Always ofcourse. 
Regardless.
171:
Today started way earlier than I would have ever wanted.

We had a worship service outside the city, so I had to wake up so early just to get everything ready. You already know how much I love sleeping, so waking up that early should honestly count as an act of love and service atp fr.

The ride there felt so long because I was still half asleep the entire time. I kept telling myself I would wake up eventually, but even when we arrived, I still felt so sleepy. On top of that, it was so hot, there were so many people around, and everything just felt overwhelming. I was tired before the day had even properly started.

But despite all of that, something strange happened.

The entire service just kept reminding me of you.

I dont even know why.

It was not just one thing.

It was everything.

Maybe it was the layout of the place.

Maybe it was because most of the people serving today were the same people who used to serve with you when you were still here.

Maybe it was because I have so many memories of seeing you in those kinds of places.

Whatever the reason was, I just could not stop thinking about you.

Everywhere I looked, I somehow imagined you there.

I could picture you laughing with everyone before the service started.

Walking around while we waited.

Talking to people here and there because somehow everyone likes you.

I could already imagine us sitting together before everything began, teasing each other over the smallest things, then suddenly becoming serious once the service started.

I even caught myself looking around for no reason, almost expecting to see you somewhere.

It is funny how memories work like that.

Sometimes all it takes is a familiar place, familiar faces, or even the same atmosphere, and suddenly your mind goes back to moments you wish you could relive.

I realized today that it was never really the place that made those memories special.

It was you.

Because if you were there today, I honestly do not think I would have noticed the heat as much.

I would not have cared that I woke up so early.

I probably would not have been so overwhelmed either.

Instead, I would have been too busy making memories with my favorite person.

We would have walked around before the service.

Found a place to sit together.

Talked about random things while waiting.

Probably gotten something to eat after.

And before I knew it, the day would have been over.

That is something I have noticed ever since we started doing long distance.

The places themselves have not really changed.

The people are mostly the same.

The services are still beautiful.

But they all feel a little different because you are not there beside me anymore.

They are still good.

They just feel like they are missing someone.

And that someone is you.

I cannot wait for the day you come home again.

Not because I need some grand vacation or some extravagant date.

I just want to experience all these ordinary moments with you again.

Going to church together.

Walking around after.

Grabbing dinner before heading home.

Listening to you tell me about your day while we drive.

Those simple moments have become some of the things I miss the most.

Today reminded me that even after all this time, you are still a part of almost every place I go.

Somehow, every familiar road leads me back to thoughts of you.

And honestly, I would not have it any other way.

I miss you so much, baby.

I cant wait until we get to wander around together again instead of me only imagining you beside me.

I love you.
Always.
Regardless.
172:
Nothing much happened today.

You were out the whole day and couldn’t really message me, so I ended up on my own for most of it. I’m not upset at you for it, and I’m not trying to make it into something bigger than it is. I understand you had things to do, and I respect that. It’s just that the day felt a bit different without our usual small conversations in between.

I tried to keep myself busy. My friends asked me to come with them somewhere, so I went along just to move around and not stay stuck in my head the whole day. I’m a little glad they invited me, because it helped break the silence and gave me something to do instead of just waiting around.

But even then, I didn’t really enjoy it in the way people probably assumed I did.

On the surface, everything was normal. I was there, I was talking, I was responding, I was laughing when I needed to. If someone looked at me, they would probably think I was fine, just having a regular day out.

But internally, it felt quieter than that.

My mind kept drifting back to you without me really trying to. It wasn’t overwhelming, just constant in the background. I’d catch myself checking my phone out of habit, not even expecting anything specific, just missing the usual rhythm of hearing from you during the day. It made everything else feel a bit less grounded.

It’s a strange feeling, being physically present somewhere but mentally feeling slightly detached from it. Like you’re participating, but not fully connected to what’s happening around you.

I don’t think it’s sadness in a heavy sense. It’s more like absence. Like something familiar that I’m used to having throughout the day wasn’t there, and because of that, everything else felt a little less complete than usual.

I kept thinking about how different it feels when we’re able to talk even for a little bit during the day. Not even long conversations, just small check-ins. It changes the way everything else feels. It makes the day feel shared instead of separate.

Without that, the day just feels like I’m moving through it on my own, even if I’m physically with other people.

And I guess that’s what I noticed most today.

Not that anything was wrong, and not that anything was bad, just that I missed you in a very quiet way throughout everything.

Not dramatic, not emotional in a loud way, just steady and present in the background of everything I did.

I’m not trying to guilt you for being busy, and I don’t want you to feel like you did something wrong. I just wanted to be honest about how today felt for me, because I think it’s better when I don’t keep that to myself.

Anyway, that’s really all there is to it.

I hope your day went okay wherever you were, and that you weren’t too tired by the end of it.

We’ll talk when you’re back. And I’ll be here when you are.

I love you.
173:
I’m just glad that we’re somehow finding our way back to our normal selves again.

I know things aren’t exactly the same, and I know it would be unrealistic to expect everything to instantly go back to how it was after everything we’ve been through these past few days. Moments like those leave little marks on both of us. They make us a little more careful with our words, a little quieter than usual, a little unsure of ourselves at times. I think that’s normal. Healing isn’t something that happens overnight, and rebuilding that sense of comfort takes time.

But despite that, today gave me hope.

It reminded me that no matter how difficult some days become, we always seem to find our way back to each other.

And I’m really thankful for that.

I missed us.

The version where conversations feel natural again.

Where there isn’t a heavy silence sitting between every sentence.

Where you can laugh freely, and I can hear that familiar tone in your voice that always makes me smile.

I didn’t realize just how much I missed that until today.

These past few days were exhausting, not because I ever got tired of loving you, but because I hated feeling disconnected from you.

I hated ending calls with a heavy heart.

I hated overthinking.

I hated knowing that both of us were carrying emotions that neither of us really wanted to carry.

Because at the end of the day, all I’ve ever wanted is for us to be each other’s safe place.

I never want our relationship to feel like another burden you have to carry.

I want it to be the place where you can finally breathe after a long day.

The place where you can laugh without thinking.

The place where you can be completely yourself.

And I want that for us just as much as I want it for you.

Today reminded me why I love the ordinary parts of our relationship the most.

Not the big milestones.

Not the grand gestures.

Not the dramatic moments.

Just us.

Watching movies together until one of us starts getting sleepy.

Talking about absolutely everything and somehow never running out of things to say.

You telling me stories from your day while I listen like they’re the most interesting thing in the world.

Me randomly asking you the most unnecessary questions just because I like hearing your answers.

You complaining about work, practicum, or something that annoyed you, and me pretending to make it worse just to hear you react.

Those are the moments I miss the most.

These simple, quiet moments are the ones that make me feel closest to you.

I miss hearing your laugh.

I miss hearing you ramble.

I miss you interrupting the movie because you suddenly remembered something you wanted to tell me.

I miss teasing you until you call me annoying.

I miss talking until neither of us notices how late it has become.

I miss falling asleep knowing that we spent the day exactly how we wanted to.

More than anything, I just miss my baby.

I know life has been busy.

I know there are days where all you want to do is come home and sleep.

And I know there will be more days like that.

But I’m okay with that.

Because I’m not chasing perfection.

I’m not asking for every day to be exciting.

I’m not asking for hours and hours together every single day.

I just want us.

Whether that means watching a movie.

Talking for a few hours.

Rotting in the call while we both doom scroll on our phones.

Or simply hearing your voice before you fall asleep.

That has always been enough for me.

I’m excited for us to have those days again.

I’m excited to spend time with you without feeling like something is sitting in the background waiting to be talked about.

I’m excited to laugh with you again until our stomachs hurt.

To argue over movie characters.

To listen to your random thoughts.

To hear you complain about something small and somehow turn it into a thirty-minute conversation.

I miss all of it.

I miss every little part of us.

And I think these past few days reminded me of something important.

No matter how difficult things get, no matter how many misunderstandings we have, no matter how tired or overwhelmed life becomes, at the end of it all, you are still the person I want to come back to.

You are still the person I want to spend my days with.

You are still the person I picture whenever I think about my future.

And even after everything, if you asked me today whether I would still choose you, my answer would still be the same.

Without hesitation.

Every single time.

So let’s slowly find our way back.

There’s no need to rush it.

We’ll laugh again.

We’ll have our boring days again.

We’ll watch movies until one of us falls asleep again.

We’ll talk about everything and nothing at the same time again.

And one day, these difficult days will just become another chapter we look back on, grateful that we chose to get through it together.

I really missed you, my love.

And I’m so happy that, little by little, I’m getting my baby back.

I love you more than these letters could ever fully explain.
174:
My baby woke me up earlier than usual today, but I decided to go back to sleep for a little while because I slept really late last night and I could barely keep my eyes open. I kept telling myself, "thirty more minutes," because I genuinely needed the rest.

But those thirty minutes felt surprisingly long.

I woke up again not because my alarm went off or because I was finally well rested, but because I missed you FR.

I don’t even know how to explain it.

I just reached a point where I thought, "okay, I’ve slept enough. I need to hear my baby."

So I grabbed my phone and called you.

Looking back, it’s actually funny. I was still tired, I hadn’t even eaten breakfast yet, and I probably should’ve gotten out of bed first. But somehow, hearing your voice felt more important in that moment than eating or doing anything else.

That’s just what you’ve become to me.

You’re the first person I naturally want to spend my day with.

And I don’t think I’ll ever get tired of that feeling.

I knew you also had to sleep early because of practicum the next day, so I wanted to make the most of whatever time we had together. There was no pressure to do anything special. I just wanted to be with you while I still could before another busy day took you away from me.

We continued watching the series we’ve been following, one of the many unfinished shows we somehow keep collecting. I still find it funny how we always end up starting something new before finishing the last one, but I honestly don’t mind. It gives us more things to look forward to together.

What I love most isn’t even the series itself.

It’s watching it with you.

Hearing your reactions.

Listening to your little comments in the middle of an episode.

Pausing because one of us suddenly has something random to say.

Teasing each other over the characters.

Trying to predict what happens next and almost always getting it wrong.

Those little moments somehow make every movie and every series feel so much more memorable.

Today wasn’t filled with anything extraordinary.

We didn’t go anywhere.

Nothing huge happened.

There weren’t any grand surprises or unforgettable events.

It was just a quiet day spent with the person I love the most.

And somehow, those are always the days that stay with me the longest.

I’ve realized that I don’t really need exciting plans to feel happy.

I don’t need constant adventures or something new happening every day.

If I get to spend my time with you, even if we’re just watching another episode of a series or talking about random things in between, the day already feels complete.

I think that’s one of my favorite things about us.

We’ve never needed to force fun.

We’ve never needed to constantly entertain each other.

We can simply exist together, and somehow that’s already enough.

That kind of comfort is so rare, and I’m grateful we have it.

Before I knew it, it was already time for you to rest.

I know practicum has been taking so much energy from you lately, and as much as I always want more time with you, I also want you to get the rest you deserve. So even though I always miss you the moment you fall asleep, I’m happy knowing you’re taking care of yourself.

I hope you know that every little bit of time we spend together matters to me.

Whether it’s eight hours or just two.

Whether we watch a whole series or only half an episode.

Whether we spend the call talking nonstop or simply sitting quietly together.

None of it ever feels ordinary to me because I’m spending it with you.

Today was simple.

Quiet.

Peaceful.

And honestly, I wouldn’t have wanted it any other way.

Thank you for another day with you, baby.

I love you, and I already miss you again.
175:
Today started with my baby waking me up again through a call.

This time, though, I learned from yesterday.

Yesterday I made the mistake of going back to sleep after you woke me up, and even though it was only for a little while, I ended up missing you so much that I woke up just because I wanted to hear your voice hihi. So today, when my baby called, I didn’t even think about going back to sleep.

Sleep can wait.

My baby cannot.

I was still a little sleepy, of course, but I knew I’d rather spend those extra hours with you than spend them asleep. Mornings have never really been my thing, you already know that, but somehow they’ve become so much easier whenever they start with you.

Almost immediately, we continued watching your favorite series.

I find it funny how invested you are in it. You get so excited over every little scene, every plot twist, every character, and somehow I end up paying just as much attention because I’m also watching you while we watch the show.

Today we managed to watch four whole episodes.

Four.

I don’t even know how the time passed so quickly.

It’s always like that whenever I’m with you. What feels like an hour somehow turns into half the day, and before I realize it, we’re already saying goodbye because you have to rest or because one of us has something else to do.

I really enjoyed the series too.

It’s genuinely good.

But if I’m being honest, I think my favorite part wasn’t even the show itself.

It was watching you enjoy it.

Seeing you get excited over the scenes.

Hearing the way your voice changes whenever something interesting happens.

Listening to your little theories about what’s going to happen next.

Watching you react, laugh, complain, or get emotionally attached to the characters.

I don’t know.

There’s just something about seeing you genuinely happy that makes me happy too.

Sometimes I catch myself smiling, not because of what’s happening on the screen, but because I’m looking at you instead.

Because I get to witness those little moments where you’re completely yourself.

Comfortable.

Excited.

Cute without even trying.

Those moments always remind me why I love spending time with you so much.

I’ve realized that one of my favorite things in this relationship is simply getting to witness your happiness.

It doesn’t even have to involve me.

Whether you’re excited about a series, talking about something you love, laughing over something I didn’t even notice, or rambling about whatever is on your mind, I genuinely enjoy watching you enjoy life.

I think that’s what love slowly becomes.

You stop chasing big moments all the time, and instead you find yourself appreciating the little expressions on the other person’s face.

The little laughs.

The little smiles.

The tiny moments of excitement.

Those become enough.

And today was full of those moments.

I know I say this a lot, but I really do love simple days like this.

No pressure.

No rushing.

No misunderstandings.

Just us, spending hours together doing something you enjoy.

And somehow, that already makes my whole day feel complete.

I hope you know that your happiness has become one of my favorite things to witness.

I’ll always cheer for the things that make your eyes light up.

I’ll always make time for the little things that make you excited.

Because seeing you smile will never be something I get tired of.

I love you so much, baby.

Thank you for another quiet, simple day that somehow became one of my favorite ones.

And thank you for waking me up again.

I promise I’ve learned my lesson now.

If my baby calls, I’m getting up. 

mwamwa wuv you.
176:
I knew I was wrong, and I knew it even while everything was happening. I just couldn't handle what I was feeling properly, and instead of slowing down and communicating it the way I should have, I let my emotions take over. From there, everything just spiraled, and before I knew it, we were both hurting.

I'm not going to sit here and pretend that everything is okay, because it's not. And I'm also not going to try to justify what I did or explain it away as if that somehow makes it hurt less. I was wrong, and I'm genuinely sorry for that.

I think we're both tired.

Tired from everything that's happened, tired from carrying emotions that neither of us really knows what to do with anymore, and tired from trying to figure out where we stand while also trying to survive everything else life is throwing at us. I know that doesn't excuse my actions, but I think it explains why things have felt so heavy lately.

The truth is, I never wanted today to happen the way it did.

I never wanted us to hurt each other.

I never wanted us to become people who struggle to understand one another, because if there's one thing I've always believed about us, it's that beneath all the misunderstandings and all the difficult moments, we've always cared deeply for each other.

That's why today hurts so much.

Because even after everything, I still care.

I still care about how you feel.

I still care about whether you're okay.

I still care about us.

I know apologies don't instantly fix things, and I'm not expecting this letter to suddenly make everything better. I know trust, comfort, and peace don't come back overnight. All I can do right now is be honest with you and take responsibility for my part in what happened.

I'm sorry.

Not because I want to move on from this quickly, but because you deserve to hear me say it clearly.

And as much as I'm hurting right now, I know you probably are too.

I don't know what happens next.

I don't know if we'll eventually find our way back to what we were, or if things have changed too much for that. But if there's one thing I hope for, it's that we don't leave this unfinished.

I hope that whatever happens, whether we find our way back to each other or whether we end up walking different paths, we talk about it properly.

I hope we don't leave each other with unanswered questions, unsaid feelings, or words we were too afraid to say.

Because after everything we've shared, after everything we've been through, I don't want our story to become something that was left hanging.

I'm sorry for today.

And despite everything, I still hope we find our way to a place where we can look at each other again without pain, without anger, and without regret.

That's all I really want right now. 

I love you
177:
Today was the hardest day we've had in a very long time.

Today, we ended things.

Even writing that sentence feels strange.

I don't think either of us woke up today expecting that this would be where we'd end up. If anything, I think we both wanted the opposite. We both wanted to keep holding on, to keep fighting, to keep believing that love alone could carry us through everything.

And maybe that's what makes today hurt so much.

Because despite everything, despite all the difficulties, despite the exhaustion, despite the distance, despite all the things life has placed in front of us, we still love each other.

That was never the problem.

If anything, love was the one thing we never lacked.

We talked for a long time.

Not to hurt each other.

Not to blame each other.

Not to decide who was right or wrong.

We talked because we owed each other honesty.

We owed each other the truth about how tired we've both become, how difficult things have been, and how sometimes loving someone and being able to sustain a relationship with them are two different things.

Especially when that relationship exists through screens, time zones, missed calls, exhaustion, responsibilities, and a future that neither of us can fully control right now.

So today, we made a decision.

Not because we stopped caring.

Not because we stopped choosing each other.

But because maybe, for now, this is the kindest thing we can do for ourselves and for each other.

We decided to stay friends.

And I know some people might not understand that.

Some people might think that if you truly loved someone, you either stay together or walk away completely.

But I don't think love has ever been that simple.

Because how do you suddenly become strangers to someone who has been your first thought in the morning and your last thought at night?

How do you stop caring about someone whose happiness you've spent so much time protecting?

How do you pretend not to miss someone who became part of your everyday life?

You don't.

At least, I don't think we can.

So instead of forcing ourselves to become people we're not, we decided to keep the connection.

To still be there.

To still care.

To still support each other.

Just without the expectations and emotional weight that we've both been carrying for so long.

And maybe that's okay.

Maybe love isn't always about holding on as tightly as possible.

Maybe sometimes it's about loosening your grip, not because you want to let go, but because you don't want to hurt the person you're holding.

I won't lie and say I'm okay.

I'm not.

Because if I could choose, I would choose you every single time.

I would choose the late-night calls.

The movies.

The arguments.

The long letters.

The overthinking.

The waiting.

The distance.

I would choose all of it, if it meant getting to keep you.

But loving you has also taught me something else.

It has taught me that sometimes loving someone means wanting peace for them, even when that peace doesn't look the way you originally imagined.

And despite everything that happened today, there was one thing that brought me comfort.

We didn't close the door.

We didn't erase what we had.

Instead, we made a promise.

That if the time ever comes when we're both in the same place in life, when we've both found our footing, when everything that life has thrown at us finally settles, and when we're together in person again, then maybe we'll give ourselves another chance.

Not because we're holding each other hostage to a future promise.

Not because we're waiting around and refusing to live our lives.

But because what we had mattered enough that neither of us wanted to say that this was the absolute end.

And I think that's beautiful in its own painful way.

Because after everything we've been through, after all the love we've shared, after all the versions of ourselves we've witnessed, we still looked at each other today and thought,

"Maybe, someday."

I don't know what tomorrow looks like.

I don't know what next week, next month, or next year will look like either.

All I know is that today, I didn't stop loving you.

I just loved you differently.

And maybe that's the hardest part of all.

Thank you for everything you've been to me.

Thank you for every ordinary day that somehow became extraordinary because you were there.

Thank you for every call, every movie, every argument we survived, every laugh, every late-night conversation, and every version of yourself that you trusted me enough to love.

And if one day life becomes kinder to us, if one day we're both standing in the same place, wanting the same things, with the same certainty we once had, then I hope we'll find each other again.

Until then, I'll still be here.

Just a little differently than before. 

I love you, still, always, 
and regardless of what happens next.
178:
I don't really know what to say after everything.

I think I'm just confused.

I've read all your words over and over again, and I don't know what I'm supposed to feel. Part of me wants to say that everything is okay, because that's the only thing I know how to do right now. Not because I truly understand everything that happened, or because the pain is gone, but because I don't know what else to say.

I guess all I can tell myself is that we'll get over this eventually.

I don't know how.

I don't know when.

And if I'm being honest, I don't even know if I want to.

Because getting over something means accepting that it happened, accepting that things changed, and I don't think I've fully accepted any of that yet.

Right now, everything just feels strange.

When we're talking, when we're in a call, when I can hear your voice, I somehow feel okay. Not because all the problems disappear, but because you're there, and for a little while, I don't have to think so much.

But when the call ends, and the silence comes back, I don't really know what to do with myself.

That's the part that's been getting to me.

I don't cry.

I don't panic.

I don't even know if I'm necessarily sad in those moments.

I just go numb.

The night becomes quiet, and suddenly I'm left alone with all these thoughts, all these feelings, and somehow none of them make sense. I don't know what I'm supposed to feel anymore. I don't know if I'm grieving, hoping, accepting, or just trying to survive one day at a time.

I keep trying to find the right emotion, the right reaction, the right thing to say to all of this, but I can't.

All I know is that I miss you.

I miss what we were.

I miss the certainty of waking up and knowing exactly who I was to you and who you were to me.

And maybe that's what hurts the most.

Not that I stopped loving you.

Not that you stopped caring.

But that we're now standing in this space where neither of us really knows what happens next.

I know we'll eventually get through this somehow.

Everyone says that.

Time passes, people adapt, life moves forward.

But right now, sitting in the silence after everything that's happened, I don't really feel strong or wise or accepting.

I just feel confused.

And when the night comes, I just feel numb.

Maybe that's okay for now.

Maybe I don't need to have all the answers tonight.

I just wanted you to know how it feels on my side.

Because despite everything, despite all the confusion and all the uncertainty, I still care enough to tell you the truth.

And the truth is, I don't know what to do, what to think, or what to feel.

I just know that I miss you.
179:
Today was cute.

I stayed up very late for my baby today, and honestly, I don't regret it at all.

We just spent the night doing what we've always been good at doing together: watching movies after movies, talking in between scenes, laughing at random things, and somehow making hours feel like minutes. It was simple, but it felt so familiar.

And I think that's what made today so special.

After everything that has happened, after all the conversations we've had, after all the decisions we've made and the paths we've chosen, we still found ourselves here, spending time together the exact same way we always did.

For a little while, it felt like nothing had changed.

There was no pressure.

No heavy conversations.

No trying to figure out what comes next.

Just us.

Watching movies together, commenting on scenes, making fun of characters, and enjoying each other's company like we always have.

And honestly, I missed that.

I missed feeling like we could just exist together without thinking too much.

I missed laughing with you.

I missed hearing your reactions to everything.

I missed feeling like, even if just for a few hours, the world outside of us didn't matter.

Eventually, I got sleepy and decided to rest.

But then, a few hours later, my baby woke me up again.

And honestly, I smiled the moment I realized it.

I don't know if you missed me so much that you couldn't wait any longer, but that's exactly what I'm choosing to believe.

So of course I answered.

And then somehow, just like that, we spent another five hours together.

Five more hours.

Watching more things.

Talking about random topics.

Laughing.

Sharing little moments that probably don't seem important to anyone else but somehow mean everything to me.

There's something so comforting about the fact that we can spend so much time together and never really run out of things to do, or even if we do, never run out of reasons to stay.

And then, eventually, I could hear it.

That familiar shift in your voice.

The slower replies.

The little noises.

The sleepy sounds.

And then eventually, the soft snores.

I know I say this a lot, but I genuinely think that's one of the cutest things in the world.

There's something so intimate and comforting about staying with someone until they slowly drift into sleep.

Hearing them fight it.

Hearing them slowly give in.

Knowing that they feel safe enough to fall asleep with you still there.

So I stayed.

And somewhere between listening to your little noises and your soft snores, I ended up falling asleep too.

Apparently, I fell asleep so hard that I overslept and ended up being late to the function I was planning to attend.

Which, honestly, is kind of funny.

I don't even think I was mad about it.

Because if I'm going to oversleep, then falling asleep while listening to my baby sleep is probably one of the better reasons.

Today reminded me of something I've been feeling for a long time.

I just want to cuddle you.

Not in some grand, romantic movie scene kind of way.

Just in the simplest way possible.

I want to lie beside you after a long day.

I want to listen to you talk until you get sleepy.

I want to watch movies while you're half asleep on my shoulder.

I want to wake up because you decided to wake me up.

I want to exist in the same space as you without needing anything else.

And the thing that makes me smile the most is knowing that one day, we're going to get that.

One day, there won't be calls ending because someone has to sleep.

There won't be screens.

There won't be imagining what it would feel like.

We'll just be there.

Together.

And honestly, after today, that future doesn't feel impossible.

It just feels like something worth waiting for.

I miss you.

And today, for a little while, I felt like I had my baby back.

I love you.
Always.
Regardless of what happens next.
180:
Today was quiet.

Nothing much really happened, but I think that's okay. Not every day has to be exciting or memorable for it to matter.

My baby had a long day today, and knowing that she has another long day waiting for her tomorrow, I already knew that we'd probably have to keep things short. And honestly, I'm okay with that.

I'd rather have a tired version of you for a few hours than not have you at all.

We still managed to spend some time together, and lately I've been learning to appreciate those little pockets of time even more. Sometimes it's not about how long we spend together, but the fact that we still choose to show up for each other despite everything else going on in our lives.

I know you've been tired.

I can hear it in your voice sometimes.

I can tell when your replies become shorter, when your eyes start getting heavy, when you're trying your best to stay awake even though your body is begging you to rest.

And honestly, I don't want you to fight that.

I don't want you to stay awake for me if what you really need is sleep.

If anything, I think there's something really sweet about knowing that even when you're exhausted, you still choose to spend whatever energy you have left with me.

That means more to me than staying up for hours ever could.

Today wasn't filled with movies or deep conversations or anything particularly special.

It was just one of those days where life happened.

You were tired.

I understood.

And somehow, that still felt like love.

Because love isn't always about the big things or long conversations.

Sometimes it's just saying, "I'm tired, but I still want to spend a little time with you before I sleep."

And I think that's beautiful.

Besides, tomorrow is another day.

You'll be home earlier, and selfishly, I'm already looking forward to that.

Maybe we'll finally watch a movie.

Maybe we'll spend hours talking about absolutely nothing and somehow turn it into a conversation about everything.

Maybe we'll complain about our days.

Maybe we'll laugh over something stupid.

Or maybe we'll just sit there and enjoy each other's company.

Honestly, I don't really care what we do.

I just miss spending time with you.

I miss those moments where it feels like the rest of the world pauses for a little while and it's just us again.

So tonight, I'll let my baby sleep.

I'll let you rest.

And I'll look forward to tomorrow, hoping for a little more time, a little more laughter, and a little more of us.

Sleep well, baby.

I'll see you tomorrow.

wuvv you.
181:
Hi baby,

I've been thinking about what you said earlier, about not wanting to give me false hope.

And I just wanted to tell you, gently, that you don't have to worry about that with me.

I know why you said it. I know you said it because you care about me, because you don't want me to hold onto something that isn't there, and because the last thing you'd ever want is to hurt me more than I already am.

But the truth is, I'm not holding onto the kind of hope that you're scared of.

I'm not secretly thinking that everything is okay, or that we're going to wake up tomorrow and magically become what we were before. I think a part of me has already accepted that things changed, and that we made the decision we made because we both felt like we had to.

That doesn't mean I don't love you.

It just means I'm trying to love you honestly now.

The only hope I'm keeping is a very quiet one.

It's not a hope that controls me, or stops me from accepting reality. It's just the thought that maybe one day, when we're both in a different place in life, when we're both okay, when we're together in person again, and when everything that pulled us apart isn't as heavy anymore, maybe we'll look at each other and decide that we still want this.

And if that day never comes, then that's okay too.

Because right now, what matters to me is that you're still here.

That I still get to hear your voice.

That I still get to watch movies with you.

That I still get to laugh with you, tease you, listen to you complain about your day, and stay in calls with you until one of us falls asleep.

I'm not doing these things because I'm waiting for a reward at the end.

I'm doing them because it's you.

Because despite everything, spending time with you still feels like one of the safest and happiest parts of my day.

So please don't feel guilty when we call.
