Don't overthink when we say "baby."

Don't be scared when we say "I love you."

I'm not keeping score.

I'm not secretly hurting every time we have a good moment together.

If anything, I'm grateful for those moments.

Because after everything we've been through, I still get to know you, to talk to you, to be part of your life in some way.

And honestly, that's something I don't want to take for granted.

I know we're both confused.

I know we're both hurt.

And I know neither of us really knows what the future looks like.

But I promise you this:

I'm not staying because I'm trapped by hope.

I'm staying because I care about you.

And as long as you're still okay with this, then I am too.

So please, don't worry about me.

I don't want you to feel guilty every time we're happy together, or every time we act like we used to for a little while.

For now, I just want to appreciate that somehow, after everything, I still get to say goodnight to you.

And that's enough for me.

I love you, my sweet girl.
182:
We managed to sneak in a movie, it was about time we watched this movie hehe.

I liked it. I thought it was good, it kept me interested the whole time, and I was having fun trying to predict what would happen next. My baby, on the other hand, did not enjoy it nearly as much.

To be fair, it was already nighttime for you by the time we watched it, which probably made everything ten times scarier. I could tell. Every little sound, every suspenseful scene, every time the music got louder, you were already preparing yourself for the worst.

And then, after the movie ended, my baby wanted to watch another movie just to forget about the scary one.

So cute.

There's just something so adorable about seeing you get scared over the smallest things. The way you react, the way you suddenly become extra cautious, the way you need something soft and comforting afterward. I know you probably weren't having fun being scared, but from my side, it was impossible not to find you cute.

I would've loved to stay up and watch another movie with you too. Honestly, I would've watched the most boring movie ever if it meant helping you forget the scary one.

But then my niece got home, and suddenly the house became a lot busier than I expected. So unfortunately, we didn't get to continue our little movie marathon.

And that's okay.

Because even if we didn't get to watch another movie, I still got to spend time with you.

I still got to stay with my baby.

And that's what mattered to me.

So instead of watching something else, I just stayed with you until you fell asleep.

I kept you company.

We talked a little.

We stayed in the call.

And I just wanted to make sure that you didn't feel alone with all the scary scenes still running through your head.

Because as cute as I find scared baby, I also know that being scared at night genuinely sucks.

And if all I could do was stay there and make you feel a little safer, then that's exactly what I wanted to do.

I think moments like this remind me of how much I love taking care of you.

Not because you can't take care of yourself, because I know you absolutely can. But because there's something so natural about wanting to make things easier for you, wanting to comfort you, wanting to stay a little longer just so you can sleep peacefully.

I wouldn't have wanted to spend tonight any other way.

So yes, maybe we only got one movie in.

Maybe my baby spent half of it terrified.

Maybe we didn't get to continue our plans.

But in the end, I still got to stay with you until you drifted off to sleep.

And somehow, that's always one of my favorite parts of the day.

Sleep well, my poor, scared baby.

I'll be here the next time you decide to watch a horror movie and immediately regret it after.
183:
Today felt full.

It's funny because if someone asked me what we did today, I'd probably say, "Nothing much." We didn't watch a movie, we didn't do anything particularly exciting, and we didn't really have any big plans. But somehow, today ended up being one of those days that stays with me.

We spent most of our time just being with each other.

And that's always been enough for me.

We talked, stayed in the call, did our own things, and just existed together. No pressure to constantly entertain each other, no need to fill every silence. Just knowing that you're there somehow makes everything feel lighter.

I've always loved that about us.

We've never needed to do anything big to enjoy each other's company. Sometimes the best moments are the ones where nothing really happens.

Eventually, my baby got sleepy, and so did I.

I swear, hearing your little sleepy noises has some sort of effect on me. The moment your voice starts getting softer, your replies become slower, and you start making those tiny sounds you don't even realize you're making, I immediately start feeling sleepy too.

So while you drifted off, I ended up taking a nap as well.

After a while, I dropped the call, thinking that was probably how our day was going to end.

And then, a few hours later, I suddenly found my baby calling me again.

The funny part was that there were so many people downstairs at that exact moment, so the second I saw your name pop up, I practically rushed upstairs just so I could answer properly.

And when I finally picked up, I immediately knew something was wrong.

My poor baby had been woken up at four in the morning by her friends for absolutely no reason.

I could hear it in your voice.

You weren't just sleepy.

You were annoyed.

Frustrated.

Irritated in that specific way where you're too tired to even properly explain why you're upset.

So I did what I had to do, I stayed.

I didn't ask a million questions.

I didn't try to fix anything.

I just stayed with you.

I talked softly.

I reassured you.

I told you that it was going to be okay, that you'd eventually fall back asleep.

I gave you kisses.

And somehow, little by little, my baby started calming down.

And eventually, just like I knew you would, you fell asleep.

I don't know why, but moments like that always remind me of how much I care about you.

Not because I did anything extraordinary.

I didn't.

I just wanted you to feel less alone in that moment.

And if staying awake with you while you were upset made things even a little bit easier, then I was happy to do it.

I really wish I could have stayed longer.

I wanted to.

But unfortunately, I had somewhere I needed to be.

Tonight was our night out with the friend group.

And it was fun.

We laughed.

We sang.

We played music.

We went to the same places we've gone to so many times before.

The same roads.

The same late-night spots.

The same motorcycle rides.

The same guitars.

The same songs.

Despite genuinely having fun, despite laughing and enjoying myself, I couldn't shake the feeling that someone was missing.

You.

Everywhere I looked, there was a memory of you.

The night sky reminded me of you.

The cool breeze while riding reminded me of you.

The sound of the guitars reminded me of you.

The conversations reminded me of you.

I kept imagining how it would have been if you were there.

You sitting across me.

You singing along.

You laughing at something stupid one of us said.

You holding onto me during the motorcycle ride.

You being part of all of it.

And suddenly, all those familiar places didn't just feel nostalgic.

They felt incomplete.

It's strange.

You can have a good night and still miss someone terribly at the same time.

Those two feelings can exist together.

And tonight, they did.

I'm really grateful that I got to spend today with you.

I'm grateful that I got to comfort you when you needed someone.

I'm grateful that even after all this time, hearing your voice still feels like home.

But tonight also reminded me of something I've always known.

I don't just miss talking to you.

I miss experiencing life with you.

The ordinary parts.

The late nights.

The motorcycle rides.

The music.

The laughter.

The silence.

All of it.

No matter how much fun I have, no matter how beautiful the night is, and no matter how many people surround me, there's always a part of me that wishes you were there too.

I miss you, baby.

I always will.
184:
Nothing really happened today.

My baby was sleepy, and I think that's partly because of me.

I woke up late.

And I know you were probably waiting for me, or at least hoping I'd wake up sooner. By the time I finally called, you already sounded tired. Maybe bored too. And I don't blame you for that.

The truth is, I wasn't really in the best state either.

I had been arguing with my parents before we called, and even though I tried not to bring that energy with me, I could feel it lingering. I was irritated, frustrated, and honestly just didn't have the emotional energy to deal with everything all at once.

And I hate that.

Because if there's one person I never want to give that version of myself to, it's you.

You didn't do anything wrong.

You were just there, being you.

And I was carrying emotions that had nothing to do with you.

By the time I started feeling okay again, by the time I felt like I could finally be present and give you the version of me that you deserve, you had already fallen asleep.

I couldn't be upset about it.

If anything, I just felt bad.

Because you had a long day.

You were tired.

You deserved to rest.

And the last thing I wanted to do was wake you up just because I finally sorted myself out.

So I didn't.

I just let my baby sleep.

And as much as I wished we could have spent more time together today, I think letting you rest was the right thing to do.

Sometimes love isn't staying up longer.

Sometimes it's not asking for more time.

Sometimes it's just looking at the person you care about, seeing that they're exhausted, and deciding that their rest matters more than your wants.

So that's what I did.

Today wasn't our best day.

It wasn't filled with movies, long conversations, or anything particularly memorable.

But that's okay.

We're allowed to have days where we're tired.

We're allowed to have days where life gets in the way.

We're allowed to have days where things don't go exactly how we wanted them to.

And tomorrow is another day.

So baba I'm sorry.

I'm sorry for waking up late.

I'm sorry for carrying my frustrations into our time together.

And I'm sorry that today didn't turn out the way I wanted it to.

I'll make it up to you tomorrow.

Hopefully with more time, a better mood, maybe a movie, and most importantly, all of my attention.

Sleep well baby.

You deserve the rest.
185:
A lot of things happened, and for a moment, it felt like we were about to lose everything we still had left of us.

I really thought that this was it.

That after everything we've been through, after all the conversations, all the calls, all the movies, all the late nights and soft moments, we were going to cut every connection we still had.

That scared me more than I know how to explain.

Because the truth is, I never stopped.

I never stopped caring.

I never stopped loving you.

And I never stopped hoping, not the kind of hope that expects you to come back tomorrow, or next week, or because I somehow deserve it. Just the kind of hope that exists when you love someone deeply enough that a part of you can't help but believe that maybe, somehow, someday, life will be kinder to both of you.

I know where we are.

I know what we decided.

And I know that things aren't the same anymore.

But if there's one thing I've never lied about, it's this: I really do love you baby.

I don't know how to turn that off.

I don't know how to suddenly look at you and see just another person.

Because you're not.

You've been my home for so long that even now, after everything, hearing your voice still feels like coming home after a long day.

And maybe that's why I kept trying.

Not because I wanted to force us back into something.

Not because I wanted to ignore the reasons why we ended.

But because losing you completely felt so much heavier than accepting that things had changed.

And I know that might sound selfish.

Maybe it is.

But it's the truth.

Because even if we stay like this, even if we never put labels on what we have ever again, even if all we do is continue calling each other, watching movies, staying in silence together, falling asleep in calls, and being part of each other's lives in whatever way we're still allowed to be, I would still choose that.

I would.

Because what we have, even now, still means more to me than the idea of starting over with someone else.

People always say that you should move on, that you should find someone new, that you should let go.

But I don't want a different person.

I don't want a new relationship.

I don't want to replace what we had with something else just because that's what people expect.

If my choices were between having some perfect, normal relationship with someone else, or having this, with you, I would choose this.

Every single time.

Because at the end of the day, it's still you.

It's still your voice I want to hear.

It's still your day I want to ask about.

It's still your laugh that makes me feel okay.

It's still your sleepy little noises that make me feel sleepy too.

It's still you.

And maybe that's not practical.

Maybe that's not logical.

But love rarely is.

I don't know what the future looks like for us anymore.

I don't know if we'll ever find our way back to each other.

I don't know if one day we'll look back at all of this and smile, or if we'll just quietly carry it with us forever.

But what I do know is that today reminded me of something I've never really forgotten.

I love you.

And no matter what we call what we have now, no matter what happens next, I'm grateful that somehow, after everything, I still get to have you in my life.

And for now, that's enough.
186:
Today feels different.

I tried to get my baby back.

Not back in the way we used to be, not back into a relationship, not back into pretending that everything that happened never happened. But somehow, I got back the thing I was most scared of losing.

You.

And honestly, that's enough for me.

I missed you so much, baby.

I missed spending time with you without feeling like every conversation was our last. I missed watching movies with you, hearing your little comments during the scenes, hearing you laugh, hearing you get annoyed at characters for no reason. I missed spending hours with you and not realizing how much time had passed.

I missed being able to just exist with you.

I know we're not together.

I know what we decided, and I understand why we decided it.

But I'd be lying if I said I didn't spend the past few days terrified that I was going to lose even this version of us. Because as much as I wanted us back, what scared me the most was the thought of losing you completely.

And somehow, today reminded me that I still have you.

Maybe not in the way I used to.

Maybe not in the way I wish I could.

But I still have you.

And honestly, I think that's why I'm so relieved.

I can't wait to watch movies with you again.

I can't wait to spend your whole night with you again.

I can't wait to be there after your work, after school, after practicum, after every tiring day where all you want to do is complain, rot in bed, and have someone stay with you.

I miss staying with you until you fall asleep.

I miss hearing your sleepy voice.

I miss hearing all your stories about your day, even the boring ones.

I miss spending hours doing absolutely nothing and somehow feeling like it was the best part of my day.

And maybe that's what I've realized.

Even if we're not together, even if we don't know what the future looks like, I still want to be here.

Because at the end of the day, it's still you.

And having this version of us, where we still get to call, watch movies, laugh, complain, and be there for each other, means so much more to me than pretending I don't care.

So thank you, baby.

Thank you for still being here.

Thank you for letting me have these moments with you.

I missed you so much.

And tonight, I just feel relieved that somehow, after everything, I still get to spend time with my favorite person.
